data.narrative:
DroneShield is a public-stage defense and security company founded by Brian Hearing and John Franklin, having raised over $100M to date. The valuation universe comprises 10 comparable companies: 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private counterparts including Evolv Technology, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, and Shield AI.

Peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The Defense & Security sector contains 26 same-sector peers overall, but the filtered set yields insufficient datapoints: only 1 company at the same stage, 0 at adjacent stages, and 0 in a similar valuation tier. A median derived from the full 26-company sector set would lack precision given the heterogeneity in business model, deployment maturity, and revenue stage across defense contractors. The analyst therefore cannot triangulate a defensible valuation range via comparable-company analysis using the available narrow-filter dataset.

Without successful application of peer-median methodology, alternative approaches—including precedent transactions, DCF modeling, or asset-based valuation—would be required to establish a triangulated range. Key uncertainties remain: the specific revenue run-rate and profitability trajectory of DroneShield relative to the identified public and private peer set, and whether the 2 public comparables or 5 named private peers represent true operational or financial analogues. Additional financial and operational metrics on target company and peers are necessary to proceed with rigorous valuation triangulation.
